To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
photosynthesis can be modeled as a multisubstrate ordered enzyme reaction with a single substrate binding site for CO2.

(1) photosynthesis is a multisubstrate ordered mechanism with RuBP binding first and CO2 binding second; (2) photosynthesis is limited by light at low CO2 and limited by CO2 at high light; (3) the maximum carboxylase turnover is 3-6 s-1; (4) the maximum efficiency of light utilization is 0.5; (5) the maximum carboylase efficiency is 0.05-0.1 mol

the development of a mathematical model of photosynthesis based on a mechanistic analysis of the carboxylation process and the regeneration of RuBP.
the effects of the state of activation and turnover rate of RuBP carBoxylase on the rate and efficiency of photosynthesis.

the model provides a mechanistic description of photosynthetic CO2 assimilation, and that it can provide a basis for the analysis of the effects of environmental factors and plant species on photosynthetic rate.

the rate of photosynthetic carbon fixation depends on the relative capacities of the two reactions involved, the carboxylation reaction and the regeneration of RuBP, and on the concentrations of CO2 and RuBP, and that the rate of the carboxylation process itself is determined by the concentration of the substrate CO2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a simple mechanistic model of C3 photosynthesis based on an ordered multisubstrate reaction can be used to describe many features of photosynthesis.
the rate of photosynthetic CO2 assimilation depends on the balance of the carboxylation and regeneration potentials of RuBP.
photosynthesis is a multisubstrate ordered process in which RuBP carboxylation is the rate-limiting step.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the efficiency of light use in photosynthesis approaches a maximum as the photon flux density is decreased and the carboxylation capacity of the plant is saturated.
the rate of photosynthetic CO2 assimilation can be described by an equation that is based on the kinetics of RuBP carboylase.
photosynthesis in the C3 pathway is limited by the capacity for regeneration of the substrate RuBP, which is dependent on the rate of light utilization.
